text:
### Issue: "Payment Processing Slow"  
**Symptoms:** FPS transfers taking >15 minutes, BACS delayed  
**Steps:**
```
1. Check payment queue
curl https://api.firstuk.bank/pps/queue-length

2. If queue growing
Monitor: kubectl logs -f deployment/pps | grep "pending"

3. Check if database is bottleneck
psql -U postgres -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event_type='IO';"

4. If high I/O wait
Increase database resources: kubectl set resources deployment/ams --limits=memory=4Gi,cpu=2

5. Monitor recovery
Watch queue decrease: watch 'curl https://api.firstuk.bank/pps/queue-length'

6. If not improving
Escalate to database team (see Step 6)
```

raw_entities.name: Payment Processing Slow
raw_entities.description: A performance degradation incident affecting Faster Payment Service (FPS) transfers and BACS payments, characterized by transfers taking longer than 15 minutes to process. The incident involves monitoring payment queue length, database I/O wait events, and resource constraints on the payment processing system.
context: FPS transfers taking >15 minutes, BACS delayed
If queue growing Monitor: kubectl logs -f deployment/pps | grep "pending"
If high I/O wait Increase database resources: kubectl set resources deployment/ams --limits=memory=4Gi,cpu=2

raw_entities.name: Check Payment Queue
raw_entities.description: Initial detection step to assess the payment processing queue status by querying the payment processing system API endpoint. This is the first diagnostic action in the Payment Processing Slow incident response procedure.

raw_entities.name: Monitor Payment Queue Logs
raw_entities.description: Conditional investigation step executed when the payment queue is growing, using Kubernetes logs to identify pending payment transactions in the payment processing system deployment.
context: If queue growing Monitor: kubectl logs -f deployment/pps | grep "pending"

raw_entities.name: Check Database I/O Wait Events
raw_entities.description: Diagnostic query executed against the PostgreSQL database to determine if I/O wait events are causing the payment processing bottleneck. Identifies whether database resource constraints are the root cause.
context: Check if database is bottleneck psql -U postgres -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event_type='IO';"

raw_entities.name: Increase Database Resources
raw_entities.description: Containment and recovery action triggered when high I/O wait is detected on the database. Increases memory and CPU limits on the application management system (AMS) deployment to resolve resource constraints.
context: If high I/O wait Increase database resources: kubectl set resources deployment/ams --limits=memory=4Gi,cpu=2

raw_entities.name: Monitor Queue Recovery
raw_entities.description: Post-remediation monitoring step to verify that the payment queue is decreasing and the incident is resolving. Continuously polls the payment processing system API to track recovery progress.
context: Monitor recovery Watch queue decrease: watch 'curl https://api.firstuk.bank/pps/queue-length'

raw_entities.name: Escalate to Database Team
raw_entities.description: Final escalation action executed if the payment queue does not improve after resource increase. Transfers incident ownership to the database team for deeper investigation and remediation.
context: If not improving Escalate to database team (see Step 6)
